title: Kandinsky 6.0 Video — a new lineup of open-source models that generate video with synchronized sound
key_facts: Kandinsky 6.0 Video is a lineup of two models that generate video with synchronized sound: Pro (29 billion parameters) and Lite (3 billion).
Code and weights are released under the MIT licence, so anyone may use them free and build products on them.
Both make clips of up to five seconds with dialogue, music and ambient sound, with lip movements matched to speech, from text or a first frame.
Lite is adapted to consumer Nvidia cards from the RTX 5060 Ti to the RTX 5090.
The developers say Pro beats the open-source LTX 2.5 in visual and speech quality, trails only MiniMax H3 among open models, and beats Veo 3.1 Fast on image animation.
Reinforcement-learning post-training cut the word error rate in generated speech by 47% for Pro.
Weights are on Hugging Face and code on GitHub.
quote_evidence: Kandinsky 6.0 Video is a new lineup of models that generate video with synchronized sound, with the code and model weights released under the MIT license: anyone can use the models free of charge and build their own products on top of them.
The maximum duration of a clip with sound is five seconds, and the developers plan to increase it over time.
In side-by-side human comparisons, the Pro model clearly outperforms its predecessor, Kandinsky 5.0 Video Pro, across all evaluation criteria.
why_it_matters_hint: A free, self-hostable video-with-sound generator, though quality claims are the developers' own.
notes: Reads as a developer announcement; comparisons are the developers' own. The article does not name the organisation behind Kandinsky.
